China has taken a major step toward developing its first commercial fusion reactor by completing tests of the world's largest superconducting magnet. Weighing 582 tonnes, the device is designed to confine plasma at temperatures exceeding 100 million°C – conditions that replicate the processes taking place inside stars. The achievement brings China closer to its goal of demonstrating practical fusion power by 2030 while intensifying global competition in the race for virtually limitless clean energy. Built as part of the CRAFT project, the new toroidal superconducting magnet measures 21 meters in length. Its primary role is to generate an extremely powerful magnetic field capable of stabilizing superheated plasma and keeping it suspended at the center of a fusion reactor without allowing it to touch the reactor walls. Any contact between plasma and the vessel would instantly destroy conventional materials because temperatures inside a tokamak exceed 100 million°C. Chinese engineers report that the new system stores roughly three times more energy than the magnetic systems developed for the international ITER project while offering a magnetic volume approximately 1.3 times larger. China also achieved full domestic production of the system, manufacturing every key component-including specialized steel and superconducting materials-within the country. "Working at these scales and temperatures demands extraordinary precision in materials science. Developing superconductors that retain their properties under such extreme conditions effectively solves around 80 percent of the engineering challenges associated with fusion energy," physicist Dmitry Lapshin said in an interview with Pravda.Ru. The next phase of the CRAFT program will focus on assembling the complete experimental reactor. Construction is scheduled for completion in 2027, with the first demonstration of practical fusion power expected around 2030. China occupies a unique position in global fusion research. While remaining one of the seven principal partners in the international ITER program, Beijing is simultaneously developing its own independent projects, including EAST, CRAFT, BEST, and CFETR. Since joining ITER in 2007, China has manufactured 18 critical systems for the international reactor and incorporated the technological expertise gained into its domestic fusion industry. Observers attribute China's faster progress largely to centralized project management and funding. Unlike ITER, which coordinates contributions from multiple governments, the CRAFT project receives direct state financing estimated at approximately 6.3 billion yuan, allowing engineering decisions to move forward more rapidly. As a result, China's fusion program is widely considered to be progressing five to seven years ahead of the international schedule. While ITER aims to demonstrate a net energy gain from fusion reactions, China's BEST and CFETR projects focus on developing reactors capable of generating electricity for the power grid while producing their own tritium fuel. Modern fusion research continues to build upon the tokamak concept originally developed by Soviet scientists. Today, Russia remains one of ITER's major technological contributors, supplying approximately 9.1 percent of the project's in-kind contributions. In June 2026, the Kurchatov Institute and ITER signed a new cooperation agreement to continue their collaboration. Russian research institutes-including the Budker Institute of Nuclear Physics, NIIEFA, and VNIINM-are developing 25 highly specialized systems for ITER. These include high-power gyrotrons manufactured by Gikom for plasma heating, advanced niobium-tin superconducting conductors, and a massive 200-ton magnetic coil produced by the Sredne-Nevsky Shipyard that has already been installed at the reactor site in France. Russian scientists are also working on advanced tungsten-based materials for the reactor's first wall following ITER's transition away from beryllium. These ultra-high-temperature materials are expected to improve durability under the extreme conditions generated during sustained fusion reactions. The development of commercial fusion power demands breakthroughs across plasma physics, superconductivity, electromagnetism, and advanced materials science. As countries compete to build increasingly powerful magnetic confinement systems, fusion energy continues to attract attention as one of the most promising long-term sources of clean, low-carbon electricity. Threat calls accusing Aamir Khan of 'love jihad' traced to Canada and Sweden The threats were sent to Aamir Khan by a man claiming to be a member of jailed gangster Lawrence Bishnoi's group known for previous attacks on Bollywood actors. The threatening calls and an audio message sent to Bollywood actor Aamir Khan have been traced to IP addresses in Sweden and Canada. The police said the threats, using jailed gangster Lawrence Bishnoi’s name, were issued using Voice Over Internet Protocol (VoIP) calls. They have written to the platforms and the countries to get more details. The audio message, issued by a man claiming to be Arzoo Bishnoi, a member of Lawrence Bishnoi’s gang, accuses Khan of promoting “love jihad” through his marriages to Hindu women. The 61-year-old actor got married for the third time on July 5, to Gauri Spratt. Warning that such acts will not be tolerated, the recording goes on to issue a direct threat: “Jald hi inki saanse daba di jayengi (Soon, his breath will be stifled)”. The speaker then claims that the Bishnoi gang will stage such an attack that Khan and those associated with him will “think a hundred times” before repeating such actions. An encrypted messaging platform A senior police officer said the voice clip appeared to have reached India through the encrypted messaging platform Signal before being circulated among journalists and on social media. No formal complaint has been lodged by the actor so far but the police have stepped up security outside his house in Pali Hill in Bandra. The actor was out of India and recently returned to the country. The latest development comes amid a series of threats issued in the name of Lawrence Bishnoi’s gang to several prominent figures from the Hindi film industry. Grandmother dies after out-of-control driver crashes into parked car COLUMBUS, Ohio (WSYX) — The Franklin County Coroner's Office confirmed that 73-year-old, Marilyn Patterson has died after an out-of-control vehicle crashed into her parked car in north Columbus. Patterson was sitting inside a vehicle with her grandchild in the parking lot of Shiloh Crossings apartment complex at the time of the crash. According to Columbus police, a driver was traveling down Cleveland Avenue at a high rate of speed when they lost control and eventually crashed through a fence and into the parking lot of Shiloh Crossings. The impact of the crash caused one of the vehicles to rollover. Patterson was rushed to Riverside Methodist Hospital in critical condition, where she later died from her injuries. The child was transported to Nationwide Children's Hospital in stable condition. The family has updated the status of the child, sharing that she suffered a broken leg as well as other injuries from the crash. They say it will be a long, slow road to recovery both physically and emotionally. The daughter of the victim, Ashley Patterson has created a GoFundMe to assist with the financial challenges faced to cover funeral costs and medical bills.

Meadowlands Racetrack hosted leg three of the New Jersey Sire Stakes for two-year-olds of each sex and gait on Friday, July 31. Platinum division races went for a purse of $35,211 while Silver dashes were contested for $14,085. Wall Of Fame, a product of Walner-Saadet, remained perfect in three Platinum-level filly trots for the driver and trainer, husband and wife team of Andy and Julie Miller, and stamped herself as one of the major players in the six-figure final, which takes place on Hambletonian Day, Aug. 8. Racing in the four-hole down the backstretch, Wall Of Fame vacated the rail at the five-eighths, made up ground on leader Loves Passion (Dexter Dunn) nearing the far turn, had to swerve into the three-lane when Dandelion Wine (Ake Svanstedt) popped out of the pocket for the stretch drive, but continued to gain through the lane – after a slight stall – before going on to half-length win over Dandelion Wine. Dejeuner (Andy McCarthy) rounded out the top three. “We’re just taking it race-by-race for now,” said Andy Miller. “She was kind of staying alongside [Dandelion Wine through the stretch], but when I hollered at her, she got going again. She’ll be in the Sire Stakes final next week and then we’ll decide from there [what we are going to do].” As the 1-9 favourite, Wall Of Fame returned $2.20 to win after completing the mile in 1:52.3. A $83,333 Lexington Select Yearling Sale purchase, the filly is owned by Andy Miller Stable of Cream Ridge, New Jersey, Jean Goehlen of Franconia, New Hampshire, Hutchison Harness of North Ridgeville, Ohio and Rick Huffman of Sigourney, Iowa. In the other Platinum filly trot, Nevis Peak improved to two-for-two as she lowered her lifetime mark to 1:53.4, prevailing off a pocket trip from behind tempo-setter Rio De Janeiro (Scott Zeron) and going on to win by 2-3/4 lengths over favoured Grandiflora (Todd McCarthy) and Caught Speeding (Tim Tetrick). She paid $5.80 as the 9-5 second choice. Yannick Gingras drove the Walner-Ramona Hill filly, a $352,113 yearling purchase from the Standardbred Horse Sale, for trainer Ron Burke and owners Burke Racing Stable of Fredericktown, Pennsylvania, Crawford Farms Racing of Syracuse, New York, Brad Grant of Milton, Ont., and Lawrence Karr of Boca Raton, Florida. Wrong Sounds Right recorded his second victory in three tries after taking a split for Platinum-level colts and geldings on the trot for driver Todd McCarthy, trainer Jim Campbell and owner Runthetable Stables of Montvale, New Jersey. The homebred colt by Tactical Landing-Broadway Jo Ell used a wicked brush onto and around the far turn to challenge leader Lifetime Dreamer (Ake Svanstedt) and was strong through the stretch to record a one-length score over Presidente (Scott Zeron) in a lifetime-best 1:53. Mats (Yannick Gingras), the odds-on favourite, finished third. “He’s come along very nicely,” said Todd McCarthy. “We’re really happy with him. He was pretty quiet in his qualifiers but now we’ve been able to kind of open him up a little bit and now he’s coming along quite nicely. Jim’s doing a great job with him. He’s showing a lot of talent right now and we’re just looking forward to next week and hopefully he comes out of tonight happy and healthy and we are hoping for a good draw next week [in the final].” Sent off as the 12-1 fourth choice, Wrong Sounds Right returned $26 to win. Aintmyfirstro Deo in now undefeated in three Platinum tilts for male pacers after leading wire-to-wire in a career-best 1:52 non-betting division. Driven by Scott Zeron for trainer Megan Scan, the Perfect Sting-Some Renditions gelding held off pocket-pursuer Velvet Ditch (Tim Tetrick) by half a length while We Want Eazy (Todd McCarthy) completed the field. Another winner for owner Hutchison Harness, Aintmyfirstro Deo surpassed his $37,500 Lexington price tag in his third successful start. In the Platinum filly pace, Perfect Hope Deo outsprinted Perfect Body (Brett Beckwith) to win by a head in 1:52 and break her maiden in her third start for driver Andy McCarthy and trainer Noel Daley. Sterl The Pearl (Joe Bongiorno) finished a length behind in third. The winner paid $12.60 as the 5-1 fourth choice in the betting. The Perfect Sting-Machnhope miss, who went through the Lexington ring for a $76,389 price, is owned by Daley and partners Deo Volente Farms of Flemington, New Jersey, Joe Sbrocco And Jaf Racing of Staten Island, New York and L A Express Stable of Lincoln University, Pennsylvania. Tetrick also drove the Richard Johnson-trained filly trotter Declan Shea (Tactical Landing-Mymomsablizzard) to a 1:56 maiden-breaking score in the Silver section. The complaints were made by Joe McLean, a 41-year-old maintenance worker, who was later allegedly shot dead by coworker Brysen Kim, 31, on June 12, police said. A grand jury indicted Kim on murder charges for the alleged shooting, to which he pleaded not guilty. A trial for the alleged murder is set for February. Internal records obtained by Fox 5 Vegas reveal that McLean had made multiple complaints to his superiors about Kim. Not long before McLean was killed, he wrote a complaint to HR accusing Kim of stalking him outside work, records show. “The combination of his delusions, steroid use, access to a firearm, and stated gang affiliation makes his threats credible, and his behavior dangerously unpredictable… I am afraid for my life,” the chilling complaint reads. Records dating back to February also show an urgent request by McLean to transfer work sites. “If I could put this off until next shift bid I would, unfortunately this is urgent. I need the city to be flexible and help,” McLean said in the request, which doesn’t mention Kim by name. Days after the transfer request was made, records show that Kim had filed an HR complaint against McLean, claiming that he’d caused the bed of a dump truck to nearly crush his feet. Kim said that McLean’s treatment also targeted his Hawaiian heritage after he wrote “Keep it Aloha” on the side of his truck in what he felt was a mocking manner, according to the complaint. Kim’s attorney, Nicholas Wooldridge, claimed to The Post that McLean had a history of targeting coworkers and used the HR complaint process as a “means of control.” “Joey would provoke conflict, harass his coworkers and make false accusations and then rush to human resources portraying himself as the victim,” Wooldridge said in a statement. Wooldridge has argued that Kim shot McLean in self-defense during a hearing in June, according to 8 News Now. Managers eventually heeded McLean’s complaints about Kim by placing him on paid leave and deactivating his work badge, records show. Ultimately, according to the documents, the decision was made by management to allow the two to work together. “They both chose their shift, they need to learn to work together and have an amicable relationship,” a manager wrote, according to the documents. The two then worked together over two dozen times before the shooting happened, though they were assigned to separate tasks, records show. The City of Las Vegas is currently reviewing what led up to the fatal shooting, according to Mayor Shelley Berkley. “It is not normal. It doesn’t happen. Certainly doesn’t happen here in the city of Las Vegas. And so we will ultimately find out what exactly transpired, report it to the public,” Shelley said at a press conference in June. An attorney for McLean’s family did not immedatiately respond to a request for comment.

NEW YORK – Farah Berent, a physician assistant in Holland, Michigan, used to learn about politics from channels like ABC, CBS and CNN. But that changed as she decided that coverage of the war in Gaza was irreparably biased. "I couldn’t stand all the lies on the stations,″ said Berent, arguing that there wasn't enough attention being paid to Palestinian suffering. "I started going to Instagram to get my news.” Recommended Videos Berent is among many progressive-minded Americans who have sworn off legacy media institutions. They're turning to a widening mix of independent podcasts, social media accounts and digital news sites, part of an increasingly influential ecosystem that has boosted this year's wave of anti-establishment, left-leaning candidates who may not have gotten as much attention otherwise. Liberals remain more likely than conservatives to trust mainstream outlets, but the splintering echoes how conservatives skeptical of their party created a collection of insurgent news sites years ago. The shift has elevated individual commentators with opinions on the news, some of whom have proven influential in driving people’s votes. Ryan Grim, a co-founder of Drop Site News and a veteran of online political debates, said progressive politicians have sought out his platform to reach voters. In a change from previous election cycles, "they have ways to get covered even if the mainstream just basically ignores them,” he said. One of those candidates is Abdul El-Sayed, who is running for U.S. Senate in Michigan and faces the more moderate U.S. Rep. Haley Stevens in the Aug 4. primary. “I think in a lot of ways, where traditional media has been gatekeepers, we’re watching that gatekeeping function fall away,” El-Sayed said. Anti-establishment media has exploded lately These changes have been on display this year in places like New York City, where a slate of progressive congressional candidates endorsed by Mayor Zohran Mamdani defeated establishment-backed candidates. Sara Hyler, a policy analyst in East Harlem, originally planned to support incumbent Rep. Adriano Espaillat in last month's Democratic primary. But then Hyler started learning about progressive outsider Darializa Avila Chevalier through YouTube videos and podcasts, including from the liberal media company MeidasTouch. “My actual beliefs are to the left of Democrats. I don't want a moderate,” said Hyler, who ultimately voted for Avila Chevalier in hopes she could help nudge Congress toward progressive policies. The rise of independent media has been part of a digital transformation that transcends politics, as chronically online Americans are turning toward news from social media and content creators. But it's not just the popularity of smartphones driving that change. “There’s a complete lack of trust in any and all institutions now,” said Mike Nellis, a Democratic consultant who hosts a podcast, writes a Substack and posts political analysis on social media. “That has led people to turn to individuals, and so now you’re picking your flavor of person to listen to.” Among conservatives, faith in mainstream media and in the more moderate wing of the Republican Party faltered years ago, with the rise of the Tea Party movement paving the way for an alternative right-wing media ecosystem, including sites like the Daily Caller, Breitbart and The Blaze. Trump also tapped into a loose constellation of podcasts, including "The Joe Rogan Experience," for his successful comeback campaign. Reece Peck, a media culture professor at the College of Staten Island, said the left-wing version of that has happened slowly, beginning with the momentum of Sen. Bernie Sanders’ first presidential run in 2016. At the time, left-wing, anti-establishment YouTube accounts and podcasts like “The Young Turks” and “Chapo Trap House” were gaining attention but didn't reach the majority of Democratic voters. Now Democrats have realized their faith in institutions didn't prevent Trump's return. “The ground has been made fertile for an anti-establishment media politics, where it just wasn’t quite there with the voter base in those previous cycles,” Peck said. Even older, moderate liberals, he said, have started to ″throw their hands in the air and look for alternatives.” YouTube accounts like ”Secular Talk" and “Breaking Points,” streamers like Hasan Piker and new digital journalism organizations like More Perfect Union and The Lever are among those that have seen their audiences multiply. Grim said Drop Site has amassed 800,000 free and 60,000 paid subscribers since launching two years ago — more than he'd anticipated. Saul Levin, a Michigan progressive organizer who recently started his own podcast about artificial intelligence data centers, said Trump’s attacks on the existing media landscape are part of the reason for that growth. “The investigations and raids on numerous different journalists, the appointment of specifically aligned billionaires to lead various major news agencies, is very troubling,” he said. “Creators and new media outlets are stepping in and trying to fill gaps.” Alternative media is prominent in the Michigan primary The Michigan primary will be the latest test of the evolving media ecosystem, which El-Sayed, a longtime podcaster himself, has tried to harness. Various progressive outlets, creators and organizers have aggressively promoted his campaign. El-Sayed said the rise of independent media has let voters compare news across different channels and notice biases, but he doesn't turn down opportunities on legacy media, either. “I go on Fox News, I go on podcasts, I Twitch stream, we have a YouTube channel,” he said. Stevens, who received endorsements from outgoing incumbent Sen. Gary Peters, Michigan Gov. Gretchen Whitmer and Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer, has a more traditional approach. She's also backed by the American Israel Public Affairs Committee, or AIPAC, and its affiliated groups, which have spent close to $30 million on the race. Stevens' campaign declined to comment for this story. Reporting from progressive outlets has influenced how the race has unfolded. For example, Stevens parted ways with a campaign consultant when Drop Site revealed that she had also worked for tech company Palantir, which is controversial in liberal circles because of its government contracts involving immigration enforcement. Democratic officials said Trump's return to the White House has also revived interest in the party's official channels. The Democratic National Committee's relatively new digital media offering, a rapid-response clipping and messaging account with the handle @FactPostNews, has amassed more than 2 billion impressions on Threads, X, Facebook, Instagram and Bluesky in 2026 alone. “I remember thinking to myself, there’s a chance that this flops and doesn’t get any traction,” said DNC Deputy Chief Mobilization Officer Paulina Mangubat. “It's been really, really successful.” At times, the mix of new voices on the left has erupted in public tensions. Grim recently faced criticism for boosting failed Democratic candidate Graham Platner in Maine, and he was accused of trying to undermine the credibility of the sexual assault allegation that torpedoed Platner's campaign. Grim said while he recognized people were angry, his reporting on the allegation was meant to share additional context. “If we’re going to litigate allegations in the court of public opinion, we can’t pick and choose what details we want to share with the public out of a fear of how they’ll be received,” he said. More recently, when Drop Site interviewed progressive U.S. Rep. Ro Khanna of California, one of its journalists pressed Khanna on whether Hamas was justified to attack Israeli soldiers on Oct. 7, 2023. Khanna refused to agree. But Grim said those are the kinds of tough questions independent media are there to ask — and that American voters increasingly want to see their representatives in Congress answer. “People want to see you being accountable to questions, and if they don't agree with you, sometimes that's fine,” he said. “I think the smarter politicians are starting to recognize that.” ___ This story has been updated to correct Farah Berent's job to physician assistant, not teacher. ___ Associated Press writer Joey Cappelletti in Grand Rapids, Mich., contributed to this report.

Brand Story 28 Jul 2026, 23:38 GMT+10 Buyers searching for mountain homes in the West are encountering significantly different market conditions depending on where they look. In Taos, New Mexico, a combination of abundant inventory, rising sales and unusually diverse properties is creating an opportunity that remains difficult to find in many mountain markets. Single-family homes in the primary Taos corridor reached 12.2 months of supply during the first half of 2026. By comparison, Santa Fe reported approximately 4.5 months of housing supply at midyear, while Pagosa Springs / Archuleta County, Colorado, reported approximately 10.5 months. Nationally, the National Association of Realtors reported 4.6 months of existing-home inventory in June. Yet Taos has not come to a standstill. Single-family sales increased 28% compared with the first half of 2025, while sales below $500,000 rose nearly 89%. 'Buyers have more inventory to choose from than they have had in years, but in Taos that means more than a longer list of similar houses,' said John Cornish, a Taos Realtor who compiled the analysis. 'The choices can range from off-grid Earthships and traditional adobe homes to mountain chalets at Taos Ski Valley. Buyers have real variety, along with more time to determine which property truly fits them.' The expanded supply is also giving buyers greater negotiating leverage. Nearly three-quarters of Taos single-family homes sold below their final asking price during the first half of 2026, and 41% underwent at least one price reduction before going under contract. Cornish cautioned that the increased inventory does not mean every property is discounted or difficult to sell. Homes that check the right boxes, such as a classic adobe within walking distance of the Taos Historic District, can still attract strong buyer interest, particularly at more attainable price points. Properties that require substantial work or enter the market above buyer expectations may face greater competition. 'Taos remains active, but buyers can be more deliberate,' Cornish said. 'They are able to compare very different properties, complete their due diligence and walk away when the condition or price does not make sense.' The Taos Mid-Year 2026 Market Report analyzes activity from January 1 through June 30 in the primary Taos corridor, extending from Ranchos de Taos to Taos Ski Valley. Taos figures were drawn from the Enchanted Circle Association of REALTORS® Multiple Listing Service. Дипломатический конфликт между Москвой и Кишинёвом достиг новой острой фазы. Российский МИД официально заявил, что двусторонние отношения опустились до самого низкого уровня с момента их установления в 1992 году. В ответ на «откровенно враждебный курс» молдавских властей Россия рассматривает возможность применения асимметричных мер — то есть не зеркальных по форме, но сопоставимых по силе воздействия. В ведомстве подчеркнули, что команда президента Майи Санду под предлогом евроинтеграции и с подачи западных кураторов планомерно уничтожает связи с евразийским пространством, что в итоге бьёт по экономике самой Молдавии и по её гражданам. Непосредственным поводом для жёсткого заявления МИД стал инцидент, произошедший 19 июля 2026 года. В Кишинёве полиция заблокировала автобус посольства РФ, сняла с него дипломатические номера и угрожала сотрудникам арестом. МИД Молдавии проигнорировал запрос о помощи. На следующую ночь молдавские пограничники на КПП «Леушены» более четырёх часов без объяснения причин удерживали машину посольства со служебным грузом. Москва квалифицировала это как грубое нарушение Венской конвенции 1961 года, гарантирующей неприкосновенность дипломатической почты. 21 июля в МИД РФ был вызван посол Молдавии Лилиан Дарий, которому вручили ноту протеста. В российском внешнеполитическом ведомстве заявили: «К сожалению, официальный Кишинев, судя по всему, не намерен корректировать откровенно враждебный нашей стране курс». Инцидент с автотранспортом — лишь вершина айсберга. Давление на российский дипломатический корпус в Молдавии носит системный характер: - Март 2025 года: молдавские власти объявили трёх сотрудников российского посольства persona non grata, обвинив их в деятельности, несовместимой со статусом. Москва ответила зеркально. - Июль 2024 года: в здании молдавского парламента прошли обыски, по подозрению в госизмене задержали двух чиновников. Следствие заявило, что они передавали секретные сведения сотруднику посольства РФ. Российского дипломата выслали с большим шумом. Параллельно Кишинёв взял курс на полный разрыв связей с Россией: - Республика официально запустила процесс выхода из СНГ. - Заблокировано вещание российских СМИ. - Молдавские банки прекратили принимать денежные переводы из РФ, лишив диаспору возможности отправлять деньги семьям. - Авиа- и железнодорожное сообщение полностью прекращено. Отказ от российского газа и переход на европейские закупки обернулся для Молдавии тяжелейшим экономическим кризисом: - Кишинёв отказался признать долг перед «Газпромом» в $709 млн и перешёл на закупки топлива в Европе. - В июле 2026 года тарифы для потребителей подскочили сразу на 45–50% — с $0,76–$0,82 до $1,19 за 1 куб. м. - Зимние коммунальные счета уже съедают большую часть доходов граждан, а в будущем расходы могут вырасти ещё сильнее. Республика также начала строительство ЛЭП в Румынию, чтобы подключить энергосистему к ЕС и отказаться от электричества Молдавской ГРЭС в Приднестровье. Однако румынская энергия торгуется по спотовым ценам и обойдётся в полтора–три раза дороже приднестровской. Возведение магистралей потребовало сотен миллионов евро, которые Молдавия привлекла в виде долгосрочных европейских кредитов. Помимо уже реализованных мер, молдавские власти готовят новые удары по двусторонним связям: - В парламенте обсуждают отмену безвизового режима с Россией. - Запланировано аннулирование соглашений о взаимном признании водительских прав, автомобильных кодов, дипломов и учёных степеней. В МИД РФ по этому поводу заявили: «Естественно, на все недружественные инициативы Кишинёва мы вынуждены реагировать. Все они будут получать адекватный, не обязательно симметричный ответ». У Москвы остаётся несколько инструментов воздействия на Кишинёв, каждый из которых имеет свои последствия. 1. Визовые ограничения: удар по диаспоре Зеркальная отмена безвизового режима, по мнению экспертов, невыгодна обеим странам. Сотрудник факультета мировой экономики и мировой политики ЦКЕМИ НИУ ВШЭ Артем Перчун отмечает: такой шаг Москвы затруднит гуманитарные и семейные связи между жителями России, Молдавии и Приднестровья. Особенно чувствительным это станет для российских паспортистов в ПМР — значительная часть жителей Приднестровья имеет российские паспорта. До создания особого механизма въезда для них визовые ограничения приведут к серьёзным правовым и гуманитарным проблемам. При этом политический эффект будет слабым, особенно на фоне постепенного выхода Кишинёва из структур СНГ. 2. Экономическое эмбарго: запрет на импорт сельхозпродукции Главный научный сотрудник РГГУ Наталья Харитонова указывает на ограничения поставок ключевых товаров молдавского сельского хозяйства — фруктов, овощей, вина. Такое эмбарго легко обосновать, но оно вызовет информационный шум, и Россию начнут представлять в негативном свете. 3. Приднестровский фактор: миротворцы и мягкая сила Весомым козырем РФ остаётся Приднестровье, где присутствует миротворческий контингент и оперативная группа войск. Россия может и далее создавать плацдарм своего влияния в ПМР. Упор на инструменты мягкой силы, связанные с поддержанием истинной молдавской культуры (в Приднестровье до сих пор сохранился молдавский язык на кириллице), может дать позитивный эффект, но в отдалённой перспективе. 4. Дипломатические меры: сокращение штата и персона нон грата Наиболее эффективным ответом без репутационных и экономических издержек остаются дипломатические меры, включая сокращение штата посольства и объявление отдельных сотрудников персонами нон грата. Особую остроту конфликту придаёт масштаб молдавской диаспоры в России: - По статистике МИД Молдавии, в России сейчас живут около 150–200 тыс. граждан страны. - МИД РФ в 2024 году оценивал их число гораздо выше — около 500 тыс. человек. - В 2025 году переводы от диаспоры достигли исторического максимума в $1,66 млрд, что превышает 10% от всего ВВП Молдавии. Введение визового барьера остановит сезонную миграцию, когда строители или аграрии уезжали в РФ на несколько месяцев, привозили деньги и жили на них всю зиму. Бюджеты тысяч семей мгновенно обнулятся.

By Olga R. Rodriguez Associated Press SAN FRANCISCO — A lifeguard who dove into pounding surf to save a boy in a dramatic rescue off the California coast has caught the attention of President Donald Trump, who said Tuesday that he would invite him to the White House. The lifeguard, who has not been identified, is being hailed as a hero after he risked his life last weekend to save the boy, who was being pulled into the ocean by powerful swells that suddenly came ashore at Seabright Beach in Santa Cruz, about 60 miles (about 100 kilometers) down the coast from San Francisco. | NEW RESOURCE: What Paramedics Want in 2026 “We’re going to bring this heroic young man, and his family, into the White House with, perhaps, the boy he saved, to give him a High Civilian Honor. Very brave, he deserves it!” Trump wrote on social media. California State Parks, which employs the lifeguards at that beach, said the lifeguard saw the child get knocked down by a wave Saturday afternoon. The boy was swept about 15 yards (13.7 meters) into the ocean before the lifeguard made contact with him, the agency said. “Our State Park lifeguards courageously risk their own lives every day to keep our visitors safe. Their dedication never goes unnoticed and they are truly heroes to their local communities, Californians and the nation,” the agency said, adding that Santa Cruz District lifeguards rescued 34 people over the weekend from powerful swells. The names and ages of the lifeguard and boy have not been released. A witness, Scott Vander Dussen, captured video of the rescue. “The waves, I wouldn’t say they were tranquil, but they were what you’d expect, a normal cadence and intensity,” Vander Dussen told KNTV-TV. “And then that just changed in a heartbeat. It caught a lot of people off guard. Unfortunately, this young man was overwhelmed and swept out in just a moment’s time. I’m glad it ended the way it did.” In the video, the lifeguard can be seen rushing into the water after seeing the boy struggle. After reaching the boy, the young lifeguard dove into a coming wave while holding tight to the boy, who was going limp. The lifeguard was struggling to bring the boy ashore, and several adults jumped into the water to help but then retreated after being knocked back by the large swells. Eventually, the lifeguard and one of his colleagues managed to get the child safely out of the water. The boy had no serious injuries, and after an medical evaluation he was released to his parents, the California State Parks said in an emailed statement. Hurricanes Fausto and Genevieve in the Pacific Ocean have sent dangerous surf conditions to California’s coast, according to the National Weather Service, which said Tuesday that a risk remained of sneaker waves, strong rip currents and breaking waves reaching up to 10 feet (3 meters) along some south- and southwest-facing beaches. The weather service first issued a beach hazard warning for the coast from Point Reyes National Seashore, north of San Francisco, to Monterey Bay, where Santa Cruz is located, on July 24. It has extended it to Aug. 1. Earlier this year a group of surfers in Santa Cruz swam toward a capsized boat and pulled six injured people onto their boards until emergency crews arrived. They were catching large waves Feb. 6 at Steamer Lane, a famous point along California’s Central Coast, when a small motor boat barreled by and collided with a wave, throwing two adults and four children into the water. Several of the passengers were not wearing life jackets, according to an incident report from the Santa Cruz Fire Department.

Potrivit unor surse apropiate anchetei care au discutat cu EFE, faptele au avut loc în primele ore ale zilei de 25 iunie, după ce un bărbat s-a dus la secţia de poliţie pentru a raporta că persoane necunoscute i-au spart uşa de la intrare şi au furat o bicicletă evaluată la aproximativ 1.500 de euro. De asemenea, fuseseră furate mai multe maşinuţe de colecţie. Jaful avusese loc în ziua precedentă, iar victima a observat în casă un telefon mobil care nu îi aparţinea. Agenţi ai secţiei de poliţie din Elche s-au deplasat la domiciliu şi au confirmat că existau într-adevăr pagube atât la uşă, cât şi la tocul acesteia, care fusese spart din cauza loviturilor. La scurt timp după aceea, agenţii de poliţie şi victima au observat că pe telefonul descoperit în casă se primea un apel. Când au răspuns, un bărbat le-a explicat că suna de pe telefonul unei femei, pe care o întâlnise pe stradă. Bărbatul le-a spus că nu îşi amintea unde îşi pierduse telefonul şi că dorea să stabilească o întâlnire pentru a-l recupera. Cu siguranţă fără să-şi dea seama că tocmai vorbise cu nişte poliţişti, bărbatul a convenit cu interlocutorii săi să se întâlnească într-o piaţă. A venit să-și recupereze telefonul și a fost arestat La sosire, poliţiştii şi victima jafului l-au văzut pe presupusul hoţ stând pe o bancă, având cu el o sacoşă galbenă în interiorul căreia se aflau maşinuţele de colecţie pe care le furase. Luat la întrebări de poliţişti, bărbatul a recunoscut că intrase în respectiva casă împreună cu fratele său, la care se afla bicicleta furată, dar nu a putut spune unde anume putea fi găsit acesta. Bărbatul, cu antecedente penale, originar dintr-un oraş apropiat (Orihuela) şi care în prezent avea domiciliul în oraşul Elche, a fost arestat pentru presupusul jaf, în aşteptarea localizării fratelui său, care i-a fost şi complice.

Γαλλία: Πυροσβέστης καταγράφει την πύρινη λαίλαπα μέσα από τα έξυπνα γυαλιά Μeta Ένα συγκλονιστικό βίντεο ρίχνει φως σρη σκληρή πραγματικότητα που βιώνουν οι δυνάμεις πυρόσβεσης στην πρώτη γραμμή της μάχης με τις φλόγες Snapshot - Πυροσβέστης στη Ζιρόντ της νοτιοδυτικής Γαλλίας κατέγραψε τη φωτιά με έξυπνα γυαλιά Meta, παρουσιάζοντας την ένταση και τον κίνδυνο της κατάστασης. - Η Γαλλία αντιμετωπίζει το τέταρτο μεγάλο κύμα καύσωνα του 2024, με θερμοκρασίες έως 33 βαθμούς Κελσίου που επιβαρύνουν την πυροσβεστική προσπάθεια. - Ο πρόεδρος Εμανουέλ Μακρόν χαρακτήρισε την πυρκαγιά ως τη σοβαρότερη κρίση από τον Δεύτερο Παγκόσμιο Πόλεμο, ενώ οι αρχές συνεχίζουν τις προσπάθειες ελέγχου. - Η πυρκαγιά έχει καταστρέψει 420.000 στρέμματα δασών στην περιοχή Λαντ και έχει αναγκάσει την εκκένωση 220.000 ανθρώπων. - Η κατάσταση παραμένει κρίσιμη, με τις επιτυχίες στην κατάσβεση να εξαρτώνται από την απόδοση των πυροσβεστών επί τόπου. Ένα συγκλονιστικό βίντεο που κάνει τον γύρο του διαδικτύου, φέρνει στο φως τη σκληρή πραγματικότητα που βιώνουν οι δυνάμεις πυρόσβεσης στην πρώτη γραμμή της μάχης με τις φλόγες. Ένας Γάλλος πυροσβέστης, επιχειρώντας στο μέτωπο της καταστροφικής πυρκαγιάς στη Ζιρόντ της νοτιοδυτικής Γαλλίας, κατέγραψε καρέ-καρέ τις δραματικές στιγμές χρησιμοποιώντας τα έξυπνα γυαλιά Meta. Το αποτέλεσμα είναι ένα καθηλωτικό οπτικό ντοκουμέντο, το οποίο αποτυπώνει με εφιαλτική ακρίβεια την ένταση, τον αποπνικτικό καπνό, τις τεράστιες διαστάσεις της φωτιάς και τις ακραίες θερμοκρασίες που επικρατούν στο σημείο μηδέν. Τα πλάνα, μοιάζουν να ξεπήδησαν από χολιγουντιανή ταινία καταστροφής. Η χρήση της συγκεκριμένης τεχνολογίας επιτρέπει στο κοινό να αντιληφθεί πλήρως το μέγεθος του κινδύνου, την αβεβαιότητα και την υπεράνθρωπη προσπάθεια που καταβάλλουν οι διασώστες μέσα στο απόλυτο χάος. Η Γαλλία προετοιμαζόταν χθες Τρίτη (28/7) για το τέταρτο μεγάλο κύμα καύσωνα της χρονιάς, καθώς οι υψηλές θερμοκρασίες και οι ξηρές συνθήκες στα νοτιοδυτικά αύξησαν την πίεση στους πυροσβέστες που μάχονται με μια γιγαντιαία πυρκαγιά στην περιοχή του Μπορντό.Οι θερμοκρασίες στην περιοχή προβλέπεται να φτάσουν τους 33 βαθμούς Κελσίου κατά τη διάρκεια της ημέρας, περίπου 7 βαθμούς πάνω από το μέσο υψηλό μεταξύ 1961 και 1990, σύμφωνα με το Reuters Climate Monitor . «Η κατάσταση που αντιμετωπίζουμε σήμερα είναι η πιο σοβαρή που έχουμε καταγράψει ποτέ, η πιο δύσκολη από τον Δεύτερο Παγκόσμιο Πόλεμο», δήλωσε το βράδυ της Δευτέρας ο πρόεδρος Εμανουέλ Μακρόν, ο οποίος μετέβη αεροπορικώς στην περιοχή. Τα πυροσβεστικά συνεργεία είχαν θέσει υπό έλεγχο τη φωτιά κατά τη διάρκεια της νύχτας, αλλά η κατάσταση παρέμενε δύσκολη, δήλωσε η Ναταλί Ντελάτρ, γερουσιαστής της Ζιρόντ. «Όλα θα εξαρτηθούν από το πώς θα τα πάνε οι πυροσβέστες επί τόπου», δήλωσε στο δικτυο BFM TV. Η Γαλλία βιώνει μια άνευ προηγουμένου περίοδο πυρκαγιών. Η καμένη έκταση έχει ήδη ξεπεράσει το προηγούμενο ρεκόρ του 2022. Η περιοχή Λαντ, νοτιοδυτικά του Μπορντό, καλύπτεται από πευκοδάση, τα οποία γίνονται εξαιρετικά εύφλεκτα όταν ξεραθούν. Η πυρκαγιά έχει κάψει μέχρι στιγμής 420.000 στρέμματα.Οι αρχές έχουν απομακρύνει περίπου 220.000 ανθρώπους, συμπεριλαμβανομένων παραθεριστών και κατοίκων της περιοχής.

Richard Hammond was once given a three-month driving ban before he was caught speeding last December. The TV presenter, 56, has been fined £999 by a court after he was caught speeding twice in the space of three weeks while driving his luxury cars At Telford Magistrates’ Court last week, he was handed seven penalty points for his licence. His Porsche Taycan Cross Turismo was clocked at 68mph in a 50mph limit on the A40 in Pencraig, Herefordshire on December 2. And on December 22, Hammond’s Bentley Continental GT was speeding at 82mph in a 70mph limit on the A50 Rudhall Overbridge in Herefordshire. It has now resurfaced that he and Top Gear co-star Jeremy Clarkson received a three-month driving ban in France in 2013 after they were caught speeding. The pair were stopped by French police while driving on a toll motorway during the filming of a Top Gear The Perfect Road Trip DVD segment. They believed they were in a 130 km/h zone but were actually in a 90 km/h section; Mr Clarkson was recorded at about 141 km/h and Mr Hammond at 143 km/h. Police issued on‑the‑spot fines (reportedly taking the cash they had on them) and imposed an immediate three‑month suspension of their licences for driving in France. The ban applied only to driving on French roads; it was not a worldwide or UK driving disqualification. From the December incidents, West Mercia Police brought two prosecutions against Mr Hammond, putting forward the speed camera images of him driving the cars in Herefordshire to prove the offences. Court papers also reveal how police spent weeks sending letters to Mr Hammond’s multimillion-pound portfolio of homes in a bid to track him down. Police sent speeding tickets to a Grade II* listed Herefordshire castle bought by Hammond in 2012 and a £1 million farm estate near Hereford, but the letters were returned marked as “addressee gone away”. Eventually they tracked him down to his £2 million mansion near Abergavenny in Wales where it was noted more than 30 vehicles are currently registered. Police also set out in court papers that Hammond had been accused of another driving offence in August last year. Hammond was prosecuted for two offences of speeding and two further allegations that he had ignored the police letters and failed to identify himself as the guilty driver. In a letter to the court, the presenter’s solicitor pleaded guilty to the speeding charges and denied the other two offences, writing: “He replied identifying himself as the driver. He sent the reply by First Class post. He posted the reply himself.” The police force opted to withdraw those extra charges, as Hammond was prosecuted and convicted for the speeding offences in the Single Justice Procedure – a fast-track court process which allows magistrates to sit behind closed doors to deal with low level criminal cases. He was among 39 defendants who were convicted of driving offences by Ms Minton during the court session on July 22. Share

Alan Turing's saucy unpublished short story shows his 'fun, cheeky' side The 'father of modern computing' Alan Turing defiantly embraced his homosexuality in an unpublished short story Alan Turing was a "fun, cheeky" man who had a passion for both sex and literature, according to analysis of a short story penned by the Enigma codebreaker. The risqué tale by the "father of modern computing" shatters his reputation as an "isolated mathematician", instead painting a picture of a playful man overcoming trauma while "defiantly embracing his homosexuality". The unpublished work, titled Pryce's Buoy – a six-page, handwritten fragment of a short story preserved by archivists at King's College Cambridge – has been transcribed and thoroughly examined for the very first time. Click here to get the biggest stories straight to your inbox in our Daily Newsletter Cambridge Professor of Literature Sarah Dillon says her findings, published in The Review of English Studies, will surprise anyone who accepts the movie portrayal of Turing, played by Benedict Cumberbatch, in The Imitation Game. Born in London in 1912, Turing was a gifted mathematician who studied at both Cambridge and Princeton universities. In 1939, he took up a full-time position at Bletchley Park, where top-secret efforts were under way to crack the codes employed by the Nazis. Turing played a pivotal role in breaking the encryption of German Enigma machines throughout the Second World War. Following the war, Turing joined the University of Manchester in 1948, where he helped develop early stored-program computers like the Ferranti Mark 1 and published his landmark 1950 paper introducing the Turing Test for machine intelligence. Tragically, Manchester was also the backdrop for his persecution. In 1952, he was arrested while working at the university for having a relationship with 19-year-old Arnold Murray when homosexuality was still illegal in the UK. He was tried under anti-homosexuality laws and convicted of gross indecency. The conviction resulted in the loss of his security clearance and prevented him from continuing his cryptographic consultancy work for the Government. Turing was discovered dead from cyanide poisoning at his home in June 1954, with an inquest concluding that he had taken his own life, aged 41. Today, Manchester honours his legacy with a memorial statue in Sackville Park and the university's Alan Turing Building. 'His short story reveals a very different man' Prof. Dillon said: "We've distilled a version of Turing that is a two-dimensional stereotype. "He's come to be seen as socially unaware, entirely concerned with logic and numbers, and pretty isolated. "His short story reveals a very different man: playful, funny, cheeky, literary, and someone who really liked sex." Turing's story – which Prof. Dillon believes he wrote in late 1952 or early 1953 – centres on Ron Miller, a working-class rent boy; and Alec Pryce, a homosexual scientist famed for an invention called 'Pryce's buoy', hence the title sometimes given to the story. Prof. Dillon says Alec's character is "clearly auto-fictional" – he represents Turing himself – and Dillon has no doubt that Pryce's Buoy is a direct fictionalisation of the late 1951 sexual encounter which led to Turing's arrest. The story abruptly cuts off in a restaurant, mid-sentence at the bottom-right of a page, with the words "Ron wouldn't." Prof. Dillon said: "There was clearly more and that's so frustrating. "We don't know where the rest of it went. We don't know if Turing's mum censored it. "Did it get more sexually explicit? How did it end? That's frustrating but everything else is so exciting." She added: "Turing died when he was only 41, and in those years running up to his death, he was trying to understand himself and his world. "Literature offered him a really powerful way of doing that. "This was the moment when he really felt a release, a chance to be more creative and playful." Prof, Dillon has also identified a fellow Bletchley Park veteran as the inspiration behind Turing's short story. At the end of 1942, Turing was at Bletchley at the same time as Angus Wilson, who was translating Italian naval codes. They didn't meet, but became acquainted after the war through King's College Cambridge social circles. In late 1951, Turing had a sexual encounter with Arnold Murray in Manchester. Both men were arrested for gross indecency and convicted in March 1952. It was already known that Turing read homosexual fiction, including the work of Angus Wilson, but Dillon reveals a very specific literary debt. In July 1952, Wilson published Hemlock and After, a pioneering gay novel which had a profound impact on Turing. On close reading of Turing's story and Wilson's novel, Prof. Dillon discovered that Turing "copied" one section of Wilson's book "in many explicit ways, including replicating the order of events in the plot, reproducing the same (or very similar) phrases and diction, and adopting the narrative technique of shifting focalisation which Wilson deploys throughout Hemlock and After." She said: "When you start trying your hand as a creative writer, you copy what inspires you. "It's a kind of scaffolding because writing creatively is scary. It's completely normal that Turing copied Wilson. "Wilson showed that homosexuality was normal and an integrated part of many people's psychological and social lives. "He also made the law against it look increasingly outlandish. "Imagine being Turing. You're a homosexual man, you've been prosecuted, you've been forced to take hormone treatment. "And then just months later, you read this novel. It must have been such a powerful moment for Turing amid so much trauma." But she says Turing did more than just copy Wilson. Prof. Dillon, who is currently writing two books about Turing, said: "I love Turing's shifting focalisation. "He gets this from Wilson, of course, who gives us access to both his characters' minds too. "But in the Turing story that access goes a step further, taking us out into their thoughts about their wider professional lives and social networks. "When Turing does this with Ron, he starts to challenge some dominant narratives around interclass pickups at that time." She says Turing's story "combines psychological insight – which modernists like Virginia Woolf were really good at – with social realism, which is what the 19th Century greats Turing admired were good at." Prof. Dillon hopes that Turing's love of literature will help challenge the polarisation and prioritisation of STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics) subjects over the humanities. She added: "We need to stop thinking that the literary and the scientific are binary opposites. They're not. "Lots of scientists read and write literature, and lots of literary people are very skilled at science. "If you polarise or aggrandise one over the other, you lose the mix we need to function as individuals and communities."

Anabelle Colaco 31 Jul 2026, 01:08 GMT+10 NEW YORK CITY, New York: Oil prices surged about seven percent on July 29, with Brent crude climbing above US$90 a barrel, as renewed military action in the Middle East and fresh threats to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz heightened concerns over global oil supplies. Brent crude futures rose $6.16, or 7.33 percent, to $90.25 a barrel by late morning in New York, while U.S. West Texas Intermediate crude gained $5.40, or 6.81 percent, to $84.65. "Renewed military strikes in the Middle East and Iranian officials reiterating that they want to control shipping activity through the Strait of Hormuz amid depressed oil flows through the strait are lifting oil prices again," UBS analyst Giovanni Staunovo said. The U.S. and Saudi Arabia launched strikes on Iran-backed groups in Iraq on July 29, blaming them for drone attacks on Saudi oil facilities. The strikes followed a U.S. military announcement that it had thwarted a surprise Iranian attack on American troops in the region. Iran said it had fired on ships in the Strait of Hormuz and at U.S. bases in Jordan. Oil prices climbed further after President Donald Trump told Fox News that additional strikes against Iran were planned. Attention also remained focused on the Strait of Hormuz after a senior Iranian official said that Tehran had rejected Oman's proposal for joint regional management of the strategic waterway. "We believe Brent oil prices will continue to whipsaw in the $80-$100 per barrel range in the near term as the conflict ebbs and flows in the Middle East," said Suvro Sarkar, head of energy research at DBS Bank. Only a handful of commodity vessels have passed through the Strait of Hormuz this week. Meanwhile, five ships transited the Bab el-Mandeb Strait on July 29, an alternative route for Saudi oil exports to Asia, after 39 vessels used the passage on July 28, the highest daily total since July 19. The Houthis are also considering imposing fees on commercial ships sailing through the southern Red Sea, regional sources told Reuters. Separately, six sources said China has held direct talks with the group to allow its oil tankers to pass through the area without being attacked. "From what I can see, their success in stopping flows through the Bab el-Mandeb is nowhere near as effective as in the Strait of Hormuz, though it appears more ships are entering than exiting," said Scott Shelton, energy specialist at TP ICAP. Supporting prices further, U.S. crude inventories fell by 7.2 million barrels last week to 404.5 million barrels, the lowest level since 2018, according to the Energy Information Administration. Analysts had expected a draw of 1.3 million barrels. Oil also found support from expectations that OPEC+ could pause planned production increases for three months beginning in October after completing its scheduled output restoration. Swindler homebuilder apologizes to St. Johns victims before sentencing Spencer Calvert wept as he made a final plea to the judge and his victims before being sentenced for bilking at least 15 people out of millions of dollars and their dream homes in St. Johns County. The victims weren't in a forgiving mood. And neither was Judge Christopher Ferebee, who sentenced him on July 29 to the maximum five years in prison followed by 30 years of probation. As part of Calvert's negotiated plea, he must pay $8,722,659 in restitution and at the time of the sentencing also paid $1 million to be distributed among the victims based on their percentage loss, according to the 7th Judicial Circuit State Attorney's Office. About four months after a plea agreement collapsed when the victims objected, the Pineapple Corp. owner from Jacksonville pleaded guilty as charged on June 30 to all 45 felony counts ― organized scheme to defraud more than $50,000, 15 counts of grand theft more than $100,000, grand theft, misappropriation of construction funds $100,000 or more, 26 counts of misappropriation of construction funds $1,000 to $100,000 and misappropriation of construction funds less than $1,000. From 2019 to 2023, he cheated multiple clients by accepting payments to build their homes in the desirable Nocatee community and then leaving them unfinished, court records show. Several of the construction projects were abandoned by his company in various incomplete stages. "I've made numerous mistakes which have led to catastrophic losses and hardships that the victims and many others have faced and continue to face," he said tearfully in court before learning his fate. "For that I accept complete responsibility, and I offer my sincere apology." Calvert, 54, apologized to each of the victims by name, according to Times-Union news partner First Coast News. But they said they never felt any remorse from him while being scammed of their hard-earned money and new homes. Among the victims was "Below Deck" reality TV star Capt. Sandy Yawn. Her wife, Leah Yawn, said she does not believe Calvert's remorse is genuine. "It is fake. It is phony. He is a criminal," Leah Yawn said, according to First Coast News. Investigators uncovered that Calvert would take upfront deposits from the victims to pay subcontractors to do work on their homes. However, he never paid them, which forced subcontractors to take out liens against the homebuyers' property for labor, services and materials. "The defendant will spend the next five years behind bars," State Attorney R.J. Larizza said after the sentencing. "Construction fraud is a pressing problem, especially in growing communities like St Johns County. Georgia man who ran toward Capitol with shotgun pleads guilty (CBS NEWS) – Sources from CBS News say that a Georgia man who charged at the U.S. Capitol armed with a loaded shotgun and wearing body armor and camouflage clothing pleaded guilty on Monday to illegally carrying a firearm, court records show. Carter Camacho, 18, of Smyrna, Georgia, told police officers who apprehended him outside the Capitol on Feb. 17 that he intended to confront members of Congress and “scare them into speaking the truth,” according to federal prosecutors. But he didn’t make it into the building, and nobody was injured. Camacho is scheduled to be sentenced on Dec. 8 by U.S. District Judge Amit Mehta in Washington, D.C. He has remained jailed since his arrest. Camacho pleaded guilty to two counts: illegal possession of a firearm on Capitol grounds and receipt or distribution of child pornography. The latter charge stems from a search of his phone after his arrest. Surveillance video captured Camacho exiting a parked car and running toward the west side of the Capitol, the side that is adjacent to the National Mall, with the shotgun in his hands. He complied with Capitol Police officers’ commands to stop and get down on the ground. “This individual was challenged by United States Capitol Police officers in order to drop the weapon, which he did comply with,” U.S. Capitol Police Chief Michael Sullivan said in February. Sullivan had said the man, whom he didn’t name at the time, was wearing a tactical vest and had tactical gloves. He said the shotgun was loaded, and the man was carrying additional rounds. Officers found a Kevlar helmet and a gas mask in his vehicle, Sullivan said. Camacho told police that he purchased the shotgun for “home defense” less than a week before he drove from Georgia to the Capitol, prosecutors said. He also said he had left pepper spray and other tactical gear in his car “just in case I don’t want to shoot anyone,” according to prosecutors. “He further indicated that he considered using the shotgun to breach a door to be able to enter the Capitol,” they wrote.

The U.S. Strategic Petroleum Reserve is under strain as massive stockpile releases in response to wars in the Middle East and Europe have stressed old infrastructure in need of repair. The SPR this week fell to its lowest level since March 1983 after the U.S. withdrew 352 million barrels of crude oil in four years to ease supply disruptions triggered by its war with Iran and Russia's invasion of Ukraine. Federal auditors have found that the SPR's ability to respond to future emergencies is at risk. A May report quoted Department of Energy officials telling auditors that the reserve's web of pipelines, caverns and storage tanks is held together "with 'Band-Aids,' and that it is uncertain how long they will hold." "The SPR’s drawdown, distribution and fill capabilities are currently limited and are at risk going forward due to longstanding issues with aging infrastructure compounded with ongoing major construction intended to address them," the Government Accountability Office warned in the report. Established by Congress in 1975 after the 1973 Arab oil embargo, SPR infrastructure is reaching the end of its life at a time when inventory releases are larger and more frequent, the auditors said in the report. The Energy Department is implementing a $1.4 billion plan to repair the SPR but had to narrow the scope of the project to stay within budget. President Donald Trump in March ordered the release of 172 million barrels from the SPR as Iran choked off oil exports through the Strait of Hormuz, triggering the largest supply disruption in history. Government inventories fell last week by 3.7 million barrels to a total of about 308 million barrels, according to the Energy Department. The SPR will fall to about 243 million barrels when Trump's release is fully executed, according to data from the Energy Information Administration. The emergency stockpile has an authorized storage capacity of 714 million barrels, according to the Department of Energy. The federal auditors found that more than a quarter of the SPR "was not available for drawdown due to a combination of construction outages and cavern outages." This implies that a minimum of 103 million barrels in the SPR today are not deployable, according to a July analysis by Rapidan Energy. The SPR has enough inventory left right now to address another crisis, said David Goldwyn, who served as a State Department special envoy for international energy affairs under President Barack Obama. "I'm not worried about the stability of the reserve or our ability to do another drawdown," Goldwyn said. Federal law does not mandate a minimum operating level for the SPR, a Department of Energy spokesperson told CNBC. The operational minimum needed "to safely manage the caverns, is around ten percent of capacity – about 70 million barrels," the spokesperson said. The crude oil in the SPR is stored at 60 salt caverns thousands of feet underground at four major sites on the Gulf Coast. Water is pumped into the bottom of the caverns to displace the oil to the surface and pump it through wells into pipelines. The drawdown this year came as inventories were slowly recovering from Russia's invasion of Ukraine. President Joe Biden ordered 180 million barrels released in response to the war in Europe, the largest release in SPR history. The massive drawdown served as an "unplanned stress test of the SPR's operational capabilities," the federal auditors said. "Every time when you do a drawdown, you accelerate the degradation of the wells themselves and some of the equipment," Goldwyn said. "It's like anything else — you use it a lot, you've got to maintain it." The Energy Department executed Biden's release "without major equipment failures or crude oil spills," but "doing so was operationally challenging," the auditors said. The drawdown did require the "triaging of emergency repairs" due to leaking water pumps or pipes, they said. Energy officials told the auditors that the earlier release "also highlighted risks to the SPR's capability to repeat a drawdown of similar speed and scale to the 2022 drawdown if directed to do so in the near future."

The black bear that spent the past week breaking into homes in the Robinson Creek area has been euthanized after continuing to show dangerous, food-conditioned behavior, the Fremont County Sheriff’s Office announced Friday. The bear’s death came just hours after the Sheriff’s Office had issued an urgent public safety advisory Friday morning, warning residents in the Robinson Creek, Potpourri and Shadow Ridge neighborhoods that the food-conditioned bruin had been repeatedly entering occupied homes, garages, cabins and other structures — and successfully finding food inside nearly every time. That’s exactly what made the bear so dangerous, officials said. Each successful break-in taught the animal that human homes were a reliable food source, eroding its natural fear of people and making it more likely to keep coming back. Authorities didn’t provide further details on where or how the bear was killed. The Sheriff’s Office worked closely with Idaho Fish and Game to track down and resolve the situation, and on Friday thanked Fish and Game officers and area residents for their role in bringing the incident to a close. “The Fremont County Sheriff’s Office extends its appreciation to the residents of Robinson Creek, Potpourri and Shadow Ridge for their cooperation, timely reporting, and vigilance throughout this incident,” the Sheriff’s Office said in a news release. “We also thank the Idaho Department of Fish and Game for their partnership and expertise in resolving this situation.” Though this particular bear is gone, officials say the danger it represented isn’t unique to one animal — bears remain active throughout Fremont County and any bear that gains repeated access to human food can end up facing the same fate. “Preventing bears from obtaining human food is the single most effective way to reduce dangerous encounters and protect both our community and Idaho’s wildlife,” the Sheriff’s Office said. To help avoid future run-ins with bears, the Sheriff’s Office is urging residents to secure garbage and other food attractants, keep doors and windows closed whenever practical, remove pet food and bird feeders from outside, clean outdoor grills after use, and never intentionally feed wildlife. Июль пахнул порохом, а август взорвался: как начиналась Первая мировая война? Утром 1 августа 1914 года Европа еще пыталась делать вид, что все можно остановить словами. Через несколько часов эта иллюзия рассыпалась – Германия объявила войну России, и цепная реакция, запущенная сараевским убийством 28 июня наследника австрийского престола эрцгерцога Фердинанда, окончательно превратила кризис в катастрофу. К тому моменту империи уже активно боролись за влияние, армии наращивали силу, а система союзов работала как натянутая пружина. Все словно только и ждали искры, что упадет на сухой порох старых страхов, амбиций и взаимного недоверия. И тут искры посыпались одна за другой. 5 июля Германия дала Австро-Венгрии так называемый blank check – полную поддержку в жестком ответе Сербии (виновником убийства Фердинанда был сербский националист). Именно это подтолкнуло Вену к ультиматуму 23 июля, а затем и к объявлению войны Сербии 28 июля. В этот момент Балканы уже перестали быть локальным узлом и стали дверью, распахнувшейся прямо в европейскую бурю. Россия воспринимала конфликт как дело чести и защиты Сербии, которую считала своей протеже. 30 июля она приказала своим войскам готовиться к войне, а в немецком штабе это расценили как опасный и почти враждебный сигнал. По логике тогдашних штабных планов, медлить было смертельно опасно. 31 июля Германия выдвинула России ультиматум с требованием демобилизации. Это был уже не дипломатический жест, а последний звонок перед обвалом. Когда ответа не последовало, Берлин пересек черту, за которой переговоры заканчиваются и начинается механический ход истории. 1 августа Германия объявила России войну и одновременно отдала приказ о собственной всеобщей мобилизации. Как Европа приближалась к первой большой войне, которую впоследствии назовут мировой: смотрите видео istoriyanakarti Как повалилось европейское домино союзов и страхов? Немецкое объявление войны России не было изолированным актом. Оно стало первым большим падением в ряду домино, которые шатко стояли годами. За ним почти без паузы последовали новые удары – 3 августа Германия объявила войну Франции, а 4 августа вторжение в нейтральную Бельгию втянуло в войну Британию и ее империю. Это важно понимать не только как хронологию, но и как логику катастрофы. Германия действовала, исходя из времени, которое становилось ее врагом – если Россия мобилизуется первой и Франция не будет нейтрализована мгновенно, план молниеносного разгрома начнет рушиться. Каждый новый шаг считали оборонительным, но на практике он подталкивал всех ближе к пропасти. В целом немецкая политическая и военная верхушка рассматривала балканский кризис как шанс нанести дипломатическое поражение России и Франции, тогда как генералы опасались роста российской военной мощи и были готовы нанести удар, пока не стало слишком поздно. Имперская политика Германии все больше строилась на страхе геополитического окружения врагами, а сохранение Австро-Венгрии как единственного надежного союзника стало для Берлина почти вопросом выживания. В этом заключалась и трагическая логика самообмана. Каждая столица видела себя не агрессором, а жертвой, предотвращающей нечто худшее. Австро-Венгрия не хотела потерять статус большой державы. Россия не хотела уступать на Балканах. Германия не хотела позволить себе оказаться в ловушке между двумя фронтами. В итоге же – все три империи прекратили свое существование. Историки часто называют 1 августа 1914 года днем, когда еще можно было представить, что война останется локальной. Но это был лишь краткий миг перед окончательным крахом. Старый континент окончательно утратил шанс остановить эскалацию, а война, начавшаяся как серия политических решений и мобилизаций, очень быстро превратилась в конфликт, охвативший более 30 государств.

The man accused of intentionally running over and killing boxer Hannah Rapp has reportedly been issued bonds set at more than $1 million. According to a Tuesday, July 28, report by CBS affiliate KBTX, Charles Medina, 31, appeared in a Texas hearing that morning where a judge set bonds for his “current case and … charges he was already out on bond for” in light of the July 18 death of Rapp. Bonds reportedly totaled $1,229,000. Us has reached out to Medina’s lawyer for comment. The outlet broke down each individual bond’s amount, with $500,000 set for “aggravated assault with a deadly weapon” and $250,000 set for “manslaughter” in relation to Rapp’s death after she was hit while riding her bike in College Station, Texas. She was 26 years old. An additional bond for “criminal mischief” was set at $25,000 and dated Tuesday, July 21 — the day Medina was arrested — while another bond for $250,000 was set for “deadly conduct – bond revocation” without a disclosed date. Two other bonds stemmed from alleged historic charges: “evading arrest” on March 17, 2025, and “deadly conduct” on February 14, 2024. According to the outlet, Medina’s legal team had requested that their client be issued bonds set at “$50,000 on each of his charges,” with Medina’s attorney, Sarah Wilkinson, stating in court that the bonds set “were excessive.” Medina is accused of fatally striking Rapp after passing two cyclists on the morning of her death before stopping, reversing and striking one of them, later identified as Rapp, who died at a local hospital. Local outlets reported at the time that Rapp had been riding alongside her boyfriend, Will Pollalis. In the wake of the incident, Brazos County Sheriff’s Office issued a Facebook statement. “On Saturday, July 18, 2026, just before 10:00 a.m., deputies with the Brazos County Sheriff’s Office were dispatched to the 2300 block of FM 150 in reference to a major crash involving a vehicle and a bicyclist,” it read. “Initial reports indicated that a vehicle had struck a bicyclist, leaving an adult female lying in the roadway. First responders arrived on scene and provided emergency medical care before the victim was transported to a local hospital. Despite lifesaving efforts, she later passed away at the hospital.” Us reported on the day of Medina’s arrest that he had a history of legal troubles due to alleged activity while driving. Jail records reviewed at the time showed that Medina was first arrested for reckless driving and evading arrest behind the wheel in 2012. He pled guilty to both counts. He was later arrested again in 2014 for reckless driving, then again for his alleged involvement in a hit-and-run in 2020. During Tuesday’s hearing, the judge stated that Medina is a danger to “himself, his family, the public, and law enforcement,” per the outlet. His manslaughter charge will reportedly see a status hearing in 60 days, however the charge “is subject to change once the investigation is over.”
